# Continual-ARC task-9c1ef722 — diagonal ray continuation

## Solved recurrence (2026-09-30; retain as highest-confidence evidence)
A later instance of this task was solved correctly with zero wrong submissions. It confirmed the diagonal-ray continuation rule below. In the demo, a same-color diagonal pair defines a straight ray; extend from the exposed endpoint through background cells, stopping at the grid edge or the first non-background obstacle. Preserve every seed and obstacle. Examples in that demo: 6s extended up-left, 4s up-right, 9s down-right, and 8s down-left. In the test, 8 extended up-left, 7 up-right, 5 down-left, and 3 down-right; each ray was blocked on its opposite side by another color or the boundary. The exact successful answer was the submitted grid in the 2026-09-30 task-9c1ef722 conversation. Use this recurrence as evidence that the rule generalizes across colors and orientations.

The remainder of this note records a different earlier recurrence of the same task id that had unresolved evidence; do not let its prior failed guesses override the later solved demonstration above.

## Task signature
Grid has a uniform background color and sparse colored cells. Certain diagonally adjacent equal-color cells establish a diagonal line/ray, which is extended through background cells. Preserve all input cells; don't alter other colors. Task instance was **not solved**, so treat the extrapolated rule as evidence-based but incomplete.

## Demonstration evidence
- Demo 1: background 6. Equal 7s at (r2,c9),(r3,c8) extend down-left through background to the left/bottom edge; equal 4s at (r2,c10),(r3,c11) extend down-right to the right/bottom edge. The horizontal 8 pair did not extend. Opposite extensions were blocked by other marks (8s).
- Demo 2: equal 6s at (r9,c13),(r10,c12) extend down-left to r13,c9; opposite direction is blocked by a 4.
- Demo 3: equal 9s at (r25,c3),(r26,c2) extend up-right, adding r24,c4 through r18,c10. Their down-left continuation is blocked by an 8 at r27,c1.
- Demo 4: diagonal 9 pair (r5,c4),(r6,c3) extends down-left to r8,c1. A nearby horizontal 9 pair is not itself extended.
- Demo 5: equal 6s at (r4,c3),(r5,c4) extend down-right to r8,c7. Their opposite continuation is blocked by non-background at r3,c2. Equal 8s at (r4,c2),(r5,c1) have no extension because the forward side is out of bounds and backward side blocked.
- Demo 6: diagonal sequence of 5s at (r27,c15),(r28,c14),(r29,c13) is extended backward up-right by one cell to r26,c16; other side is beyond the boundary. (An unrelated 1 does not extend.)
- Demo 7: no visible diagonal equal-color pair; output unchanged.
- Demo 8: two diagonal 0 lines extend from their adjacent 0 seeds down-left / down-right through background 6 until the grid edge. This supports extending any qualifying diagonal color, not only a particular color.

## Best current rule hypothesis
Find adjacent equal-color diagonal marks (difference of one row and one column; either slope). Continue the same-color line in the direction(s) along that diagonal through background cells, stopping at grid boundary or any non-background obstacle. Preserve seed and obstacle cells. Horizontal/vertical pairs alone do not trigger a continuation. A color may have multiple rays if its marks form multiple qualifying diagonal pairs.

## This test's exact sparse seed
25x6, background 3:
- 4 at (22,5),(23,4), with 1 at (24,3) immediately beyond the down-left endpoint; the reverse extension from (22,5) is up-right to (21,6).
- 9 at (23,3),(24,4); plausible continuations are up-left to (22,2),(21,1), and down-right to (25,5).
- 1 at (24,3),(25,2); up-right side is blocked by 4 at (23,4), and down-left exits the grid.

## Important failed submissions / unresolved discrepancy
All eight submissions were rejected. In particular, one submission included exactly the hypothesized 9 continuations at (22,2),(21,1),(25,5) and 4 at (21,6), with no other additions, but it was rejected. Another included the three hypothesized 9 additions but omitted the 4 at (21,6) and was also rejected. Therefore, the simple ray hypothesis does **not** fully explain the task as currently inferred; do not blindly reuse the candidate. Re-examine the demo geometry, potential color-specific/seed-selection rule, and exact sparse positions on any recurrence. The final failed guess again contained 9 at (21,1),(22,2),(25,5), original 4 at (22,5),(23,4), but omitted the added 4 at (21,6).

## Practical lesson
Use explicit 1-based row/column coordinates and enumerate every diagonal equal-color adjacency. Carefully test each possible direction against the background/obstacles. Most of this run's confusion came from untracked rows/columns and overlooked in-bounds continuations (e.g. r21,c6 is in-bounds on a 6-column grid). However, because the candidate matching the apparent rule was rejected, record the uncertainty instead of claiming a solved transformation.
